key_insight: No single intra-patient 3D multimodal registration method is robust across datasets, with overlap-based and image-based metrics often disagreeing.
engineering_relevance: For clinical and computational imaging pipelines, this means registration systems must be selected and validated with multi-metric, anatomy-aware benchmarks rather than a single score.
method: Benchmarked classical optimization-based and modern learning-based deformable registration methods.
Compared performance across three datasets spanning synthetic deformation recovery and real clinical scenarios.
Evaluated with DSC, HD95, and MIND-SSC to capture both geometric overlap and multimodal structural consistency.
evidence_signal: Across three datasets, learning-based methods performed best on large synthetic benchmarks, while gains were limited in real pelvic registration and metric disagreement was persistent.
watch_item: Anatomy-guided methods can inflate overlap inside segmented regions while degrading global deformation quality outside those labels.
paper_title: Benchmarking Intra-Patient 3D Deformable Multimodal Image Registration
